## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Suvaṇṇamigajātaka* (Ja 359) is a narrative in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. The framing narrative is set while the Buddha was residing at Jetavana in Sāvatthī, delivered concerning a pious maiden of good family (*kuladhītā*) who was an exemplary supporter of the two chief disciples and devoted to the Three Jewels [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. The canonical verse portion opens with the phrase *Vikkama re mahāmiga* [Fausböll 1883]. At the conclusion of the birth story, the Buddha performs the *samodhāna* (tying the characters together), identifying the hunter of the past with the monk Channa, the female deer (*migī*) with the young nun, and the deer king (*migarājā*) with the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1883].

In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral records a full Sanskrit parallel preserved in the *Mahāvastu* under the title *Śiriprabha Jātaka* (Mvu 54) [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali corpus, DharmaNexus identifies twelve matching passages of internal text reuse with two sections of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (eight matches in the third volume, *Tatiyo bhāgo*, and four in the fourth volume, *Catuttho bhāgo*) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments exceeding the reporting threshold are detected by DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].
